source_text:
Τῇ
οὖν Ἀττικῇ χρηστέον πρὸς σταθμὸν καὶ νόμισμα, ἐπείπερ ἰσοδύναμός ἐστιν καὶ
ἰσοστάσιος τῇ Ἰταλικῇ ἣ καλεῖται «δηνάριον», ὡς γὰρ ἐπίπαν τοῖς Ἰταλικοῖς νῦν
χρῶνται πολλοί. Ἡ Ἀττικὴ μνᾶ στατῆρας ἔχει κεʹ· ἡ δὲ Ἰταλικὴ λίτρα στατήρων ἐστὶ
κδʹ· τῶν δὲ λοιπῶν μνῶν μυρίαι διαφοραὶ καὶ οὐδέν τι ἡμῖν ἀναγκαῖαι νῦν
ἐκτεθῆναι. Ἡ δὲ λίτρα ποιεῖ ˉγˉο ιβʹ καὶ ἡ ˉγˉο δραχμὰς ηʹ· ἡ δὲ δραχμὴ γραμμάτων
ἐστὶν γʹ· τὸ δὲ γράμμα ὀβολοὺς ἔχει βʹ· πάλιν τὸ γράμμα θέρμους γʹ, ὁ θέρμος κεράτια
βʹ, ὡς εἶναι τὴν λίτραν κερατίων αψκηʹ. ∆ιαιρεῖται δὲ ἐκ περιουσίας καὶ τὸ δηνάριον
κατὰ Ῥωμαίους εἰς μέρη αρνβʹ· ἔχει γὰρ τροπαϊκὰ δύο, νούμους τέσσαρας, ἀσσάρια
ι ʹ· ὁ δὲ νοῦμος ἔχει ὀγκίαν τῷ σταθμῷ. Τὸ ἀσσάριον διαιρεῖται εἰς ἥμυσυ καὶ τρίτον
καὶ τέταρτον καὶ ἕκτον καὶ ὄγδοον καὶ ἔνατον, δέκατον, δωδέκατον, ἑξκαιδέκατον,
εἰκοστοτέταρτον, τριακοστόεκτον, τεσσαρακοστοόγδοον, ἑβδομηκοστοδεύτερον· τὰ
δὲ μέρη ταῦτα ἰδίας ὀνομασίας ἔχει παρὰ τοῖς Ῥωμαίοις λογιστικοῖς. Ὁ τοῦ οἴνου
ἀμφορεὺς ὃν καὶ «μετρητὴν» λέγουσιν οἱ πολλοὶ ἡμιαμφόρια μὲν ἔχει βʹ ἃ καλοῦσιν
«κάδους» ὀνόματι κοινῷ Ῥωμαῖοι δὲ «οὔρνας», προύχους δὲ ἔχει δʹ, χόας ὀκτὼ οὓς
δὴ «κογγία» λέγουσιν «κάβους» δὲ ἡμεῖς· ὁ δὲ χοῦς δύναται ξέστας ʹ (τὸν δὲ ξέστην
«ἵνιον» καλοῦσιν Αἰγύπτιοι), ὡς τὸν ἀμφορέα εἶναι ξεστῶν μηʹ. Ὁ δὲ Ἀντιοχικὸς
μετρητὴς τοῦ Ἰταλικοῦ διπλάσιον. Ὁ οὖν ξέστης διαιρεῖται κοτύλαις δυσὶν ἃς
«ἡμίνας» καλοῦμεν, ἡ κοτύλη διαιρεῖται εἰς ὀξύβαφα δύο, τὸ δὲ ὀξύβαφον εἰς
κυάθους μερίζεται τρεῖς καὶ ὁ κύαθος δὲ ποιεῖ μύστρα δʹ ἃ δὴ «λίστρια» πολλάκις
ἐκάλεσαν, κοχλιάριον δέ ἐστιν τοῦ μύστρου τὸ ἥμυσυ· καὶ ὁ ξέστης ἄρα εἰς κοχλιάρια
ἀναλύεται ʹ. Καὶ τὰ ἐλαιηρὰ παραπλησίως, πλὴν ὅτι ἀπὸ τοῦ καλουμένου
«κεντηναρίου» τὴν ἀρχὴν ἔχει ὃ δὴ λίτρας ἔχει ρʹ. Ἔστιν δὲ καὶ ὁ ἐλαιηρὸς μετρητὴς
τοῦδε διπλάσιον· τὰ δὲ λοιπὰ μέτρα συνᾴδει· ὃν γὰρ λόγον ἔχει ἡ λίτρα τὸν σταθμὸν
πρὸς τὴν μνᾶν, τὸν αὐτὸν ἡ μετρητὴ λίτρα πρὸς τὴν κοτύλην ἢ τὸ ἡμίξεστον. Ὁ
Ἀττικὸς δὲ μέδιμνος Ἰταλικοὺς δύναται μοδίους ʹ, καλεῖται δὲ ὁ μόδιος «ἑκτεύς». Ὁ
μόδιος ἔχει ἡμίεκτα δύο, τὸ ἡμίεκτον ἔχει χοίνικας δʹ, ἡ χοῖνιξ δὲ ἔχει δύο ξέστας, ὡς
τὸν μόδιον εἶναι ξεστῶν ι ʹ. Καὶ τὰ λοιπὰ δὲ μέτρα τῶν ξηρῶν ὁμοίως τοῖς
προειρημένοις ὑγροῖς.

The Attic mina staters has 25; the but Italian litra of-staters is 24; of-the remaining minas myriad differences and nothing some to-us necessary now to-be-set-out. The but litra makes ounces 12 and the ounce drachmas 8; the but drachma of-grammata is 3; the but gramma obols has 2; again the gramma lupines 3, the lupine keratia 2, as to-be the litra of-keratia 1728. Is-divided but from surplus also the denarius according-to Romans into parts 152; it-has for tropaika two, nummi four, assaria 10; the but nummus has an-ounce to-the-weight. The assarion is-divided into half and third and fourth and sixth and eighth and ninth, tenth, twelfth, sixteenth, twenty-fourth, thirty-sixth, forty-eighth, seventy-second; the but parts these own namings they-have beside the Romans accountants. The of-the-wine amphora which also 'metretes' they-say the many hemiamphoria yes has 2 which they-call 'kadoi' by-a-name common Romans but 'urnae', prouchoi but it-has 4, choes eight which then 'congiia' they-say 'kaboi' but we; the but chous can xestai [blank] (the but xestes 'hinion' they-call Egyptians), as the amphora to-be of-xestai 48. The but Antiochene metretes of-the Italian double. The then xestes is-divided with-kotylai two which 'heminai' we-call, the kotyle is-divided into oxybapha two, the but oxybaphon into kyathoi is-portioned three and the kyathos but makes mystra 4 which then 'listria' often they-called, spoon but is of-the-mystron the half; and the xestes then into spoons is-dissolved [blank]. And the oily similarly, except that from the being-called 'kentenarion' the beginning it-has which then litrai has 100. Is but also the oily metretes of-this double; the but remaining measures they-agree; which for ratio has the litra the weight toward the mina, the same the measured litra toward the kotyle or the half-xestes. The Attic but medimnos Italian can modii [blank], is-called but the modius 'hekteus'. The modius has hemiekta two, the hemiekton has choinikes 4, the choinix but has two xestai, as the modius to-be of-xestai 10. And the remaining but measures of-the-dry similarly to-the having-been-said-before liquids.
pass_b_english: One must use the Attic, then, toward weight and coin, since it is equal in power and equal in weight to the Italian which is called a denarius; for in general many now use the Italian. The Attic mina has 25 staters; the Italian litra is of 24 staters. Of the remaining minas there are myriad differences, and nothing of them is necessary for us to set out now.

The litra makes 12 ounces, and the ounce 8 drachmas; the drachma is of 3 grammata; the gramma has 2 obols; again the gramma 3 lupines, the lupine 2 keratia, so that the litra is of 1728 keratia. The denarius also is divided, from surplus, according to the Romans into 152 parts: for it has two tropaika, four nummi, 10 assaria; and the nummus has an ounce in weight. The assarion is divided into a half and a third and a fourth and a sixth and an eighth and a ninth, a tenth, a twelfth, a sixteenth, a twenty-fourth, a thirty-sixth, a forty-eighth, a seventy-second; and these parts have their own namings among the Roman accountants.

The amphora of wine, which most also call a metretes, has 2 hemiamphoria, which they call kadoi by a common name, and the Romans urnae; it has 4 prouchoi, eight choes which they call congiia, and we kaboi. The chous can [blank] xestai (and the Egyptians call the xestes a hinion), so that the amphora is of 48 xestai. The Antiochene metretes is double the Italian. The xestes, then, is divided by two kotylai, which we call heminai; the kotyle is divided into two oxybapha; the oxybaphon is portioned into three kyathoi; and the kyathos makes 4 mystra, which they have often called listria; and a spoon is half of the mystron; and the xestes, then, is dissolved into [blank] spoons.

And the oily measures similarly, except that they have their beginning from the so-called kentenarion, which has 100 litrai. And the oily metretes is double this; the remaining measures agree: for the ratio the litra has in weight toward the mina, the same the measured litra has toward the kotyle or the half-xestes. The Attic medimnos can [blank] Italian modii, and the modius is called a hekteus. The modius has two hemiekta; the hemiekton has 4 choinikes; the choinix has two xestai, so that the modius is of 10 xestai. And the remaining measures of the dry, similarly to the liquids already said.

choices.why: αψκηʹ is 1000+700+20+8. Check: 12 oz × 8 dr × 3 gr × 3 lupines × 2 keratia = 1728.
